changes.balance: About 275 kb/d of WCS demand is back online. The question is how much of the discount narrowing is already priced into the near-term months.
changes.body: Quantum Commodity Intelligence reports ExxonMobil has its Joliet, Illinois refinery back in service as of about Sep 27. The underlying article is paywalled and no independent non-paywalled confirmation has surfaced. The ~275 kb/d heavy-crude buyer returns after the Sep 13 power outage. While it was offline, the Western Canadian Select (WCS) discount to West Texas Intermediate (WTI) stayed wide and under pressure; with the refinery back, that discount could narrow quickly in the near-term months.
changes.title: Joliet back in service

changes.balance: The war premium is back in the price after Friday's de-escalation fade. With Brent-WTI near $11.9, WTI is the relatively cheaper barrel.
changes.body: On Saturday Trump rejected Iran's proposed seven-day Hormuz roadmap, the deal markets had been pricing on Friday when Brent fell 2%. Brent reopened about 3% higher near $107, with WTI near $94. Underneath the price premium, physical flows keep recovering: Hormuz transits are back to about 13.5 million b/d, roughly two-thirds of the pre-conflict level, and Saudi Gulf loadings are at their strongest since the conflict began. But ship harassment stepped up (19 ships targeted in 48 hours; a tanker struck near Khasab), and the Houthis fired their heaviest salvo against Saudi Arabia since July, with Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's Hormuz-bypass hub, directly under fire.
changes.title: De-escalation bid died over the weekend

changes.balance: Tight distillate markets support synthetic crude over WCS into winter; the effect on crude exports is secondary.
changes.body: Ilsky (Krasnodar, ~130 kb/d) halted Saturday; Lukoil's Perm (~252 kb/d) halted and Novoshakhtinsk was knocked offline Friday (both single-source reports); the Moscow refinery was hit in the largest one-night drone barrage of 2026 overnight Sunday. Refining capacity is being knocked out faster than it is repaired, into a global distillate market at record stress: US retail diesel at an all-time high, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) gasoil refining margins near $95/bbl vs ~$74 in August, and New York Harbor ultra-low-sulfur diesel (NYH ULSD) at a record $113.48 on Sep 16.
changes.title: Ukraine's biggest refining-strike weekend of 2026

changes.balance: A de-escalation headline hurts the crowded WTI longs most; fresh escalation could drive a WTI catch-up rally, since WTI lags Brent by about $11.9.
changes.body: Speculators in WTI are net long 101,828 contracts (Commodity Futures Trading Commission data), the 96th percentile of the one-year range: a crowded long position that would have to unwind if prices fall. In ICE Brent, speculators hold 218,114 net long contracts after selling about 23% of their longs in a single week; that book is already de-risked.
changes.title: Positioning: WTI crowded long, Brent de-risked

changes.balance: Trade houses and producers look to be hedging the Canadian differentials into Joliet's return, but that attribution is inferred, not confirmed.
changes.body: Our Commitments of Traders (COT) model flags large, high-confidence weekly builds in commercial short positions on the ICE WCS 1A and ICE SW 1A differentials: 5,874 more short lots on WCS, 2,259 on SW. That fits traders hedging export economics or producers selling into the rally ahead of Joliet's return.
changes.title: Commercial shorts build on the Canadian differentials

changes.balance: Cross-border pipes are functionally full (~272 kb/d spare on June data) heading into the fall demand window: extra barrels clear through price (wider differentials, deeper apportionment cuts), not through spare capacity.
changes.body: Enbridge's October Mainline apportionment (official notice, Sep 16): 8% on Line 2/93 lights and 4% on Line 4/67/93 heavies at Kerrobert, plus 7% on Line 1 NGL/refined volumes at Regina (FPA) and 3% at Kerrobert (SPA). No force-majeure or leak headlines over the weekend on Keystone, Trans Mountain, or the Mainline. CER June data: Keystone at 94% of available capacity, Mainline excluding Gretna at 94.5%.
changes.title: Mainline apportioned for October

changes.balance: Bearish crude headline, bullish distillate reality: the synthetic-crude-vs-WCS dislocation widens into winter.
changes.body: Energy Information Administration (EIA) weekly report (week ending Sep 18): commercial crude stocks rose 2.97 million barrels to 426.4 million, a bearish surprise against a small expected draw; Cushing rose 2.27 million to 23.7 million. But distillate stocks fell 0.43 million barrels to 107.4 million, 12% below the five-year average, and refinery utilization dropped 2.8 percentage points to 94.0%, with Midwest refineries showing the largest drop in crude runs. That is the Joliet outage showing up in the runs data. Midwest (Petroleum Administration for Defense District 2, PADD 2) crude imports fell 595,000 b/d week over week to 2.437 million b/d; rising Canadian imports resume with Joliet's return.
changes.title: EIA: crude builds, distillate stays thin

changes.balance: Wider Merey discounts compete with WCS for the same buyers even when freight, not crude fundamentals, drives the move: any US Gulf Coast coking refinery weighing Merey against WCS sees the same heavy-sour trade.
changes.body: October-loading Merey cargo offers widened from about -$14 to about -$19/bbl vs Brent over the course of September, driven by freight, not fundamentals: the Aframax tanker rate from Jose, Venezuela to the US Gulf Coast hit $3.5 million per voyage (about $7/bbl equivalent). US imports of Venezuelan crude ran 583 kb/d in the week ending Sep 18. The Wall Street Journal reports the Pentagon-backed NABEP consortium has rigs and equipment lined up for Venezuela. Plans, not barrels.
changes.title: Merey discounts widen on record freight

flags.body: BP Whiting union (United Steelworkers, USW) talks reconvene tomorrow (Sep 29). A settlement removes the strike risk; a walkout would be Joliet in reverse: refinery demand steps off and the WCS discount widens.
flags.title: Whiting union talks tomorrow
flags.trigger: A strike authorization or walkout turns this into a ranked change; a settlement ends it.

flags.body: Syncrude's 50-day coker turnaround wraps around Oct 5 and CNRL's Horizon upgrader turnaround ends around mid-October. Both restore synthetic-crude supply, which should narrow the synthetic-crude premium over WCS into the fall.
flags.title: Synthetic crude (SCO) supply returns ~Oct 5 to mid-Oct
flags.trigger: Confirmed completion dates on either turnaround move this into the ranked changes.
